properties.name: The /readyz module is registered as its own artifact, and the core readiness artifact it had been written over is restored
properties.rationale: FOUND WHILE MERGING origin/main into #620 on 2026-09-30, by reading the export diff against main: #620's records registered the new /readyz module with add_artifact under id art:readiness, which already stood for crates/reflow2-core/src/readiness.rs (registered 2026-08-02; REALIZES cmp:readiness and cap:readiness-gating; INCLUDES from rel:v0220 to rel:v0750). add_artifact on an existing id revises it, so the core file's record was moved to the mcp file: its name, location, checksum and description changed, its release history now claimed releases shipped a file that did not exist then, and the core file was left unmodelled. The merge driver carried it through cleanly (main had not touched those properties), and reflow2_check stayed green because the moved record's checksum matched the file it now pointed at. Fixed in the RECORD only: the class is open (fact:add-artifact-on-an-existing-id-moves-that-artifact-to-another-file-and-says-nothing-2026-09-30).
properties.stands_in_for: add_artifact says so, or refuses, when the id it is given already names an artifact at a different location, instead of moving that artifact to the new file in silence
properties.subject: record
properties.summary: art:readiness is crates/reflow2-core/src/readiness.rs again, exactly as main records it, with no REALIZES cap:degraded-surface, and the Fragment its registration yielded has its title back. The #620 module crates/reflow2-mcp/src/readiness.rs is art:http-readiness, baselined, and REALIZES cap:degraded-surface.
